title: Zupee Reportedly Lays Off All Staff Weeks After AI Pivot Claim
description: Inc42 reports Zupee has laid off its entire workforce weeks after announcing an AI pivot, raising questions about the Ludo gaming startup's future.

body.text: Zupee, the Delhi NCR gaming startup known for mobile Ludo, has reportedly laid off its entire workforce and is close to shutting down, according to an Inc42 exclusive. The report comes only weeks after the company said it was exiting gaming to build AI products. It matters because Zupee was one of India's best-known casual gaming brands, and the fate of roughly $120 Mn in investor money is now an open question. Zupee did not respond to Inc42's request for comment, so much of this rests on unnamed sources.

Per Inc42, the startup has given affected employees severance covering the period until January 2027. Sources told the publication that the final round of layoffs coincided with Zupee's public AI announcement on October 16.
On that date, Zupee said it was leaving the gaming business and would build AI-led ventures, drawing on its experience of serving over 200 Mn users. It did not say what the new product would be.

One source told Inc42 there was no AI plan and that the announcement was damage control to hide a wind-down. According to the same sources, only three or four people remain, working directly with the founders. These are claims from anonymous sources, and Zupee has not confirmed them.
Inc42 reports that the October restructuring also closed other Zupee businesses. Here is what the report lists:

items: NeoAstro, the astrology platform, has been shut down.
Zupee Studio, its microdrama venture, has been shut down.
The proposed acquisition of microdrama startup Vertical TV fell through. Inc42 could not independently establish why.

body.text: The October layoffs were not the first. Inc42 says Zupee cut around 200 employees about ten months earlier, and nearly 170 before that. At its peak, the company had close to 500 staff.

Inc42 traces the decline to the ban on real-money gaming, which hit the company's revenue hard. Its casual games portfolio did not bring in enough to make up the gap, which pushed Zupee toward diversification, including microdrama.

Zupee was founded in 2018 by Dilsher Singh Malhi and Siddhant Saurabh and built its business on mobile versions of traditional Indian games such as Ludo, Snakes and Ladders and Carrom. According to Inc42, it raised over $120 Mn from backers including Z47, Orios Venture Partners, Nepean Capital, WestCap Group, Tomales Bay Capital and AJ Capital.

The biggest unanswered questions are financial. Inc42 says it is unclear what cash reserves, assets and liabilities remain. It asked investors, including Z47 Partners and Nepean Capital, whether they knew about the shutdown and layoffs, whether the AI pivot was pitched to them as a real strategy, and whether unused capital can be recovered. None responded.

Watch for an official statement from Zupee, any confirmation of a formal shutdown or liquidation, and whether investors comment on the outcome. Until then, treat the claim that the AI pivot was a cover as unconfirmed. For Indian gaming more broadly, the case shows how hard the real-money gaming ban has been on companies that relied on it.

sources.title: Exclusive: Why Zupee’s AI Pivot Was A Smokescreen For Its Shutdown
